Entries.Original: *glug glug*
I love the layered black and white in this black velvet! Sooo cute! And it's also deliciously sweet!!!
Virgin black velvet, you mean. Yours is a layered coffee drink made with a generous amount of honey and sugar.
As I recall, you have something of a sweet tooth. I am delighted to see that you are enjoying your beverage.
Yeah, this is great! I want another!
Hah... Looks like our little lady here is finally learning to enjoy herself at the bar. Welcome to the world of adults.
Supply Squad Member A
Oh, the bar's open? I heard it was going to be closed for a while.
Welcome. For a short time, I will be tending bar here in the barkeep's stead.
You're from the supply squad, right? Nice to see you. Thanks for always having our backs.
The supply squad? Then you must often be tasked with delivering supplies to the dome dwellers. Allow me to thank you for your service.
Supply Squad Member A
Oh, no, Minori, you work so much harder than me, between your squad missions and your deliveries around the base. And now even tending bar.
Nonsense, tending bar is nothing but a joy for me. Now, what can I make for you?
Supply Squad Member A
Hah, spoken just like the barkeep. A Moscow mule, please.
Here's your Moscow mule.
Fulfilling, isn't it, delivering something to its recipient? That's a feeling I understand quite well.
Supply Squad Member A
Yes, I always love that moment when the recipient smiles and accepts their package.
Supply Squad Member A
I take pride in my mission whenever I see that smile. Oh, of course, my responsibilities don't compare to what all of you have to endure, fighting on the front lines.
Oh, I don't agree.
Supply Squad Member A
Really? You don't?
Not at all. Let me tell you a little anecdote about how I started to hold delivery in such a high regard.
This story is about a happy family that came to be precisely because of delivery people.
Oh? Now that's something. Just about every bartender out there has a fascinating life story up their sleeve, just waiting to be revealed to the right customer.
Is that so? Regardless, you've piqued my interest. Mind if I listen in?
Of course not. It's a short tale, but a special one.
Minori Ohshima
One day, a certain man arrived in Hakone for work all by his lonesome.
Minori Ohshima
He was feeling lonely when he caught sight of a bar and decided to step inside. Soon, a woman walked in and took the seat beside him.
Minori Ohshima
She was a real naif, a sheltered young lady who appeared to have wandered into the bar under the impression it was a cafe.
Minori Ohshima
Noticing the girl was flustered, the man gave her a few words of advice.
Minori Ohshima
On down the line, both the man and the woman would insist that that day, that moment, was something like a fated encounter.
Sounds like quite the romantic event.
Minori Ohshima
The two chatted, and time flew by. Soon, closing time arrived. Reluctant to bid farewell to the young lady, the man mustered his courage and asked:
Minori Ohshima
"Would you like to exchange letters with me?"
Minori Ohshima
The dark cloud that had seemed to hang over the lady evaporated, and she gave him a sunny smile and a nod in reply.
Ooh, ooh... The mature encounter suddenly turned into a bittersweet love story.
Yet why did they insist on beating around the bush? They both ought to have spoken their true feelings aloud.
Minori Ohshima
Perhaps because he lived in Fukuoka, and she in Hakone. Long-distance relationships face many difficulties. Perhaps exchanging letters was an expression of their consideration for each other.
Minori Ohshima
That said, their love faced a much greater difficulty than mere distance.
Minori Ohshima
Her parents could not condone a romance with a man off the street, his background unknown. They forbade her from writing him and ordered her to sever ties.
Minori Ohshima
The man, not knowing any of this, poured his heart into each and every letter he wrote.
Did those letters reach her, though?
*scrub scrub*
His feelings most certainly did.
But how? I thought she was forbidden from writing back.
That's right, but she could not bring herself to give up on him, and she was a resourceful young lady.
Minori Ohshima
Whenever the postman was expected, she would pretend to sweep the front yard or go out for a walk and wait in front of the house.
Minori Ohshima
That way, she could accept his letters directly, before they even went into the mailbox.
I see! So that's how they were able to send letters to each other behind her parents' backs!
Minori Ohshima
Thanks to her efforts, though they communicated only through letters, the two grew ever closer.
Minori Ohshima
They longed to meet again, yet a new obstacle stood before them. He had to relocate overseas for work.
So now an ocean separates our two would-be lovers. The course of true love never did run smooth, I suppose.
Minori Ohshima
Perhaps feeling his hand had been forced by this crisis, the man resolved himself and wrote to her:
Minori Ohshima
"I will wait for you at the bar where we first met, at the same time, at the same seats."
Yet though he waited and waited, she never came.
What happened?!
He waited for as long as time would allow, but at last, the day of his departure arrived.
And then...
*bong bong*
Oh, would you look at the time. It seems closing time has come already. Let us continue this story tomorrow.
You're stopping there?!
Heh... Not bad.
Supply Squad Member A
Now I've got to come back tomorrow!
Thank you very much for spending some time with us tonight. We look forward to your next visit.
